history.summary: 11th-century Sun temple on the Pushpavati river, built 1026-27 CE under Solanki king Bhima I in the Maru-Gurjara (Solanki) style. Three axial sections: the Surya Kund (massive stepped tank ringed by 108+ small shrines), the 52-pillared Sabha Mandap and the Guda Mandap (sanctum). Its east-facing alignment lets the equinoctial sunrise illuminate the sanctum. Tradition says it commemorated Bhima I's defence of Modhera against Mahmud of Ghazni (verify). Now an ASI-protected monument with no regular worship; added to UNESCO's Tentative List on 13 December 2022. CSV TOWN/STATE FLAG: CSV row has town 'Mehsana' (the district) and puts the town name in the state column - temple stands at Modhera village, Mehsana district, GUJARAT.

name: Modhera Sun Temple
town_description: Modhera is a village in Mehsana district, north Gujarat, on the banks of the Pushpavati river. It is known almost entirely for its 11th-century Sun temple, one of India's finest Solanki-era monuments and a major heritage tourism draw near Patan.
tradition: Hinduism (Surya worship) - now an ASI-protected monument; no regular worship

travel.road: Modhera village, ~25 km from Mehsana; best reached by taxi/private vehicle (public transport to the village is limited)

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; early morning for best light, equinoxes for the sunrise alignment
visitor_information.opening_hours: Daylight hours as an ASI monument; entry ticket ~INR 25, evening light-and-sound show ~INR 30 (verify current timings and fees)
